lines: - **design-ends** A design ends when the PO says its questions are answered or stops it; the next Review archives it. → long/design-ending.md
- **design-conclusions** At its end, write the conclusions into the product log and pass them to the Sprint that asked. → long/design-ending.md
note: Long file: the whole of the old rule, word for word, with the convention numbers replaced by handles (blank page: pick the target and let the PO order the items; mark the design concluded and awaiting archival in its Now line; keep the log and all original working material together until archival and link to the originals, a summary or a commit ID alone is not enough; if a Sprint builds the conclusions link to the prototype as a specification, never leave its only copy in a Sprint folder; the material is design evidence, never an Increment; with the PO's explicit permission merge the design branch into its base and delete it, pushing needs consent; a design has no Review or Retro of its own, the first Review that can read its complete log and material in its own checkout archives it; and the rest of the rule, which the ledger holds in full).

line: - **ideo-in-every-stage** Each design stage takes its methods from the IDEO mode it stands on.

adds_to_target: Design decisions the PO makes: each stage result and entry or return (including how this round of Ideate will diverge), set or change the design goal, pick the How Might We questions that matter, choose the solution and decide between combining and a rumble, agree how real the prototype must be, decide that the design ends, and explicitly permit git actions (commit, merge, branch deletion, push) before they run.

where_else: plugins/ideo-scrum/skills/design-kernel/conventions/design-backlog-template.md has the five chapters, one per stage, and says each records what its stage produced, not the steps taken (line 8).
plugins/ideo-scrum/skills/design-kernel/SKILL.md, first paragraph, lists the renamed terms.

adds_to_target: In a design, write the half-finished work into the chapter it belongs to and update the header before a session ends or its context is shortened; Now and permission to enter or resume a stage do not by themselves authorize committing, merging or pushing; commit only if the PO explicitly recorded commit permission for it, otherwise keep the changes uncommitted and record the status and where to resume.

Sharpen the design goal during Empathize; once it is set, only the PO changes it. The questions, the map and the solution may change with what the work shows; write what changed and why in the chapter it belongs to.

line: - **ideate-arrangement** Before Ideate, the PO settles how the round diverges; until then no gathering, sketching or delegating. → long/stage-gates.md
note: The old first line design-gates (a stage permission covers only that stage's design work, not a commit, merge or push) is folded into outward-needs-po and the stage-gates long file. Long file: the four-row table (what the log holds and the check at each stage) word for word, and 'would someone who never learned design have produced the same thing?'; record permission to start Empathize when opening and no placeholder goal as a commitment; record how far git permission reaches on the stage or ending decision line; record the Ideate arrangement in chapter 3 before the solution section; choosing a solution is not permission for Prototype and a trial run is not permission for Test; the goal's exact text goes in the 1.2 table and is read before each stage decision (the Product Goal too if direction is at issue), stop if it cannot be read, the wording on the dated decision line is a record not a source, show it to the PO only when the goal changed, direction is at issue or they ask; when a stage shows an earlier answer was wrong, report it and wait for permission to return; after Test the PO decides whether to end the design or return.

line: - **small-design** A small design is still a design: keep the log, shrink each stage to a line or two, skip no stage, keep the stage permissions.
